summary: As I grew up, I saw my mango tree start flowering in January, where it used to flower during March and April. I looked at the cause behind this. Phenological mismatch, and turns out this affects more than just mangoes, like migratory birds, which is very well studied with great tits and how they adapted to it. Through my website, I intend to tell curious members of the public about how these non trivial questions like mangoes flowering early can be connected to data and explore the limits of what data can be used to prove and where it fails. We also demonstrate why we fail to capture the trend, and give a reason to the best of our abilities on why we couldnt capture a trend.
details:
1. We have a detailed user interface where he/she can ask questions and/or select variables for analysis. This gives users a glimpse into how historical data is stored and analyzed. We’ve also provided a few regions to select from, that tells user that region specific data can be utilized for analysis
    1. Data: NASA MERRA-2 monthly reanalysis (GES DISC), 1980 to 2025: air temperature (T2M), day and night temperature (T2MMAX, T2MMIN), rainfall (PRECTOTCORR) and surface sunlight (SWGDN). We fetched it through NASA Earthdata (earthaccess, OPeNDAP via pydap, xarray, h5netcdf) and stored it as cached files so the app never depends on NASA servers during use.
    2. Backend: Python 3.12 with Flask (served with gunicorn), pandas, NumPy and SciPy. Statistics: Theil-Sen slope, Mann-Kendall significance test, 95% confidence ranges, and a years-of-data-needed estimate based on Weatherhead et al. Question routing and answer wording are rule-based with fixed templates, plus a wording checker that blocks invented numbers and causal claims. No generative AI is used in the current demo.
    3. Frontend: React 18, Vite, Recharts and Lucide icons.
    4. Deployment: Vercel (frontend) and Render (backend).
    5. Development: Git and GitHub, VS Code, and more than 250 automated tests (pytest and unittest). Everything was built and run on standard Windows laptops. No special hardware was needed.
dataRefs: MERRA-2 tavgM_2d_slv_Nx (M2TMNXSLV): monthly 2 m air temperature (T2M)
MERRA-2 tavgM_2d_rad_Nx (M2TMNXRAD): monthly surface incoming shortwave flux (SWGDN)
MERRA-2 statM_2d_slv_Nx (M2SMNXSLV): monthly daily minimum and maximum air temperature (T2MMIN, T2MMAX)
NASA Earthdata Login (used to access the data)
